title: Why do Lines and Angles matter?
text: Look around you! The screen you are looking at has right angles. The bridges connecting cities rely on the precise calculation of alternate interior angles to ensure they don't collapse. Architects use parallel lines to design safe and beautiful buildings. In this chapter, we will learn the language of geometry.

title: Basic Terms and Definitions
text: A line has no endpoints and extends infinitely in both directions. A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint and extends infinitely in one direction. When two rays originate from the same end point, an angle is formed. The rays making an angle are called the arms of the angle and the end point is called the vertex of the angle.

definitions.description: Measures greater than 90° but less than 180°.
Measures greater than 180° but less than 360°.

content.title: The Clock Trick
content.text: Think of a clock. At 3:00, the hands make a Right Angle (90°). At 6:00, they make a Straight Angle (180°). Any time between 12:00 and 3:00 creates an Acute Angle!

content.display_text: Complementary Angles: Two angles whose sum is 90°.
content.related_display_text: Supplementary Angles: Two angles whose sum is 180°.

content.title: Don't Mix Them Up!
content.mistake: Students often confuse Complementary (90°) and Supplementary (180°).
content.correction: Remember: 'C' comes before 'S' in the alphabet, and 90 comes before 180 in numbers! So, Complementary = 90, Supplementary = 180.

title: Finding the Supplementary Angle
problem: An angle measures 75°. Find its supplementary angle.
solution_steps: Let the supplementary angle be x.
We know the sum of supplementary angles is 180°.

title: Adjacent Angles and Linear Pair
text: Two angles are adjacent if they have a common vertex, a common arm, and their non-common arms are on different sides of the common arm. If the non-common arms form a line, then the angles are called a Linear Pair.

title: Linear Pair Axiom
conditions: When a ray stands on a line, the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°.

title: Solving with Linear Pairs
problem: Angles A and B form a linear pair. If angle A = (2x + 10)° and angle B = (x - 10)°, find the value of x.
solution_steps: Since A and B form a linear pair, their sum is 180°.

title: Vertically Opposite Angles
text: When two lines intersect, they form four angles. The angles opposite to each other at the intersection vertex are called vertically opposite angles. The theorem states: If two lines intersect, then the vertically opposite angles are equal.

question: Two lines AB and CD intersect at O. If angle AOC = 50°, what is the measure of angle BOD (its vertically opposite angle)?
explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. Since angle AOC and angle BOD are vertically opposite, angle BOD = 50°.

title: Parallel Lines and Transversal
text:
A line which intersects two or more lines at distinct points is called a transversal. When a transversal intersects two PARALLEL lines, special angle relationships are formed:
1. Corresponding angles are equal.
2. Alternate interior angles are equal.
3. Alternate exterior angles are equal.
4. Interior angles on the same side of the transversal (consecutive interior angles) are supplementary (sum = 180°).

content.title: The Letter Tricks for Transversals
content.text:
- Look for the letter 'F' to find Corresponding Angles (they are equal).
- Look for the letter 'Z' to find Alternate Interior Angles (they are equal).
- Look for the letter 'C' or 'U' to find Consecutive Interior Angles (they add to 180°).

content.title: Assuming Any Transversal Makes Angles Equal
content.mistake: Believing that alternate interior angles are ALWAYS equal when a transversal intersects ANY two lines.
content.correction: Alternate interior angles and corresponding angles are ONLY equal if the two lines intersected by the transversal are PARALLEL. If the lines are not parallel, the angles exist, but they are NOT equal.

title: Parallel Lines Complex Problem
problem: Lines l and m are parallel, intersected by transversal t. One interior angle is 3x, and the alternate interior angle is x + 40. Find x and both angles.
solution_steps: Since lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal.
Substitute x to find angles: 3(20) = 60° and 20 + 40 = 60°

title: Angle Sum Property of a Triangle
formula: Angle A + Angle B + Angle C = 180°
conditions: The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is exactly 180°.

title: Finding a Missing Triangle Angle
problem: In triangle PQR, angle P = 45° and angle Q = 75°. Find angle R.
solution_steps: By Angle Sum Property: Angle P + Angle Q + Angle R = 180°

title: The Exterior Angle Conundrum
problem: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110°, and one of the interior opposite angles is 30°. Find the other two angles of the triangle.
solution: Let the missing interior opposite angle be x. By the exterior angle theorem, 110° = 30° + x, so x = 80°. The third angle of the triangle forms a linear pair with the exterior angle, so it is 180° - 110° = 70°. (Or using Angle Sum: 180 - (80+30) = 70°). The other two angles are 80° and 70°.

title: Chapter Summary
points: Complementary angles sum to 90°; Supplementary angles sum to 180°.
Angles in a linear pair sum to 180°.
When a transversal cuts parallel lines: Corresponding angles are equal, Alternate interior angles are equal, and Interior angles on the same side are supplementary.
Sum of angles of a triangle is 180°.
Exterior angle of a triangle equals sum of two interior opposite angles.
